# nonUrl

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a URL.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonUrl() — Checks whether a value is **not** a URL. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/url</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonUrl<T>(value: T | string): value is T;
```

`nonUrl(value)` is the same test as `!isUrl(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An `http`, `https` or `ftp` URL with something after the scheme and no whitespace anywhere. A bare host such as `"example.com"` is not one.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| string` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a URL; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonUrl("example.com"); // => true
nonUrl("https://"); // => true
nonUrl("https://exa mple.com"); // => true
nonUrl("https://example.com"); // => false
nonUrl("http://example.com/a?b=1"); // => false
```
